content:
According to Mark Gurman's latest Power On column, Apple is reportedly considering overhauling its App Store to boost the platform's potential revenue.

Apple's specific plans for the App Store remain unclear. Bloomberg reporter Mark Gurman reported that Apple wants to "find ways to improve profit margins and generate more recurring revenue," a direction largely driven by incoming CEO John Ternus and current Senior Vice President of Services Eddy Cue.

Reportedly, this effort was one of the reasons veteran employee Phil Schiller left Apple last week. Schiller stepped down from his role as Senior Vice President of Marketing in 2020 and took on an Apple Fellow role, which included overseeing the App Store as part of his responsibilities. Schiller opposed the idea:

Apple has several ways it could improve App Store profit margins. It could remove its manual app review process — an expensive process that is less effective in the age of agentic coding. However, users might not welcome further automated review, even if it helps reduce costs.

Apple could raise its developer membership annual fee, currently $99 per year. Given that many small developers already spend $200 per month on subscriptions to Codex and Claude to create apps, some might argue Apple still has room to raise prices and developers would still pay. Apple could also charge large developers monthly fees based on usage, passing some of the infrastructure costs on to them.

The end result remains unknown, but I'm personally very much looking forward to seeing what form these changes ultimately take.
